title: Chemistry — Mission 4: The Saturation Point
description: A batch of crystals grew where they shouldn't have. Figure out what happened to the solution's concentration before the next batch is ruined too.

mika.name: Ms. Mika Tan
mika.description: Has seen every solubility mistake a student can make, twice.

priya.name: Priya
priya.description: Mixed the batch and wants to know what went wrong.

solubility_chart.name: Solubility Curve Chart
solubility_chart.description: Grams of solute per 100 g water, plotted against temperature, for common compounds.

concentration_notes.name: Concentration Notes
concentration_notes.description: Molarity, molality, and percent-by-mass formulas, worked through step by step.

elements.text: I made this solution warm, like always, and now it's got crystals sitting at the bottom. Did I mess up the recipe?
Maybe not the recipe — maybe the temperature. Solubility isn't constant.

elements.prompt: Mika hands you the solubility curve chart.

options.text: "Let's check the solubility curve — solute that dissolved hot might not stay dissolved once it cools."
"The recipe must be wrong, let's remix it from scratch."

elements.text: Good, chart in hand. Let's read it correctly this time.
No chart yet — we're just guessing without it. Let's fix that.

config.question: The solubility curve shows this compound is more soluble at higher temperatures. What happens as the hot, saturated solution cools?

options.text: The solution becomes supersaturated and excess solute crystallizes out
Nothing changes — solubility is independent of temperature
The solute becomes more soluble as it cools
The solvent evaporates, concentrating the solution

config.explanation: As temperature drops below the point where the dissolved amount matches the curve's saturation value, the solution holds more solute than it can keep dissolved, and the excess crystallizes out.

config.prompt: Priya: "If I dissolve 2.0 mol of solute in 4.0 L of solution, what's the molarity, in mol/L? Just the number."
Order these solutions from least to most concentrated relative to their saturation point.

items.text: Unsaturated — can still dissolve more solute
Saturated — holding exactly the maximum dissolved solute
Supersaturated — holding more than the equilibrium maximum

elements.text: The recipe was fine the whole time — it was always going to crystallize on cooling. Next batch, cool it slowly on purpose.
We figured it out eventually, but let's read the curve before remixing anything next time.

elements.prompt: The batch mystery is solved. What now?

options.text: Show Priya how to read the solubility curve so this never surprises her again.
Log the result and move on. Good enough for today.

elements.text: So it was never broken — the curve just told me it would do exactly this. I can predict that now instead of panicking.

ending.title: Saturation Solver
ending.description: Diagnosed the crystallization from the solubility curve alone and taught Priya to read it herself.

ending.title: Batch Logged
ending.description: The mystery is resolved and logged. The deeper curve-reading lesson can wait.
